document.title: Eval: one rubric grader per case, expected.md rewritten by hand
document.summary: The two free-text Muse graders become one rubric call that answers yes or no per expected.md item and checks each lookFor bullet at head. Every expected.md is rewritten from its pull request, and case.json drops claims for together and apart pairs.
document.why: A census of 133 graded runs found the grading itself was the biggest source of noise: a missing claim counted up to three times, free-text majors swinging about 50% between runs, graders that never saw expected.md, and grading that cost more than producing [session](source:s1).

sources.label: Claude Code session · Oct 23
sources.gist: Redesign the eval grading so it is simple and effective: deterministic pass or fail stays, one rubric call per case with must, good, mustNot lists and a bounded lookFor truth check, prose quality as lints, every expected.md rewritten from the PR by a trusted model, rescore grades saved reviews, validate on saved reviews before producer runs.

sources.label: Eval: one rubric grader per case, read from expected.md
Eval: rewrite every expected.md from the pull request
Eval: the grader accepts the main fact; shorter Must items

lookFor: The [brief](source:s1) asked to generate or validate the case.json lists from expected.md. At head there are no lists in case.json: scripts/eval/case.ts reads the Must, Good, and Must not bullets from expected.md at load time, so expected.md is the only source.

The [brief](source:s1) asked to extend together and apart pairs from each Groups section. A sweep of 133 saved reviews with --rescore --no-graders showed three of the new pairs failing most good reviews on a judgment call, so they were dropped; the audit-vs-page-objects apart pair on cigster-99 stays and fails 5 of 23 saved reviews because the skill folds the report into the page objects.
The [brief](source:s1) shows the case line as mustNot 0. At head it prints mustNot hits over items, mustNot 0/5, so a case with no Must not list reads differently from one with no hits.
Grader verdicts still do not change the exit code. caseFailed in scripts/eval/result.ts reads only producerError, validateError, and checks.failures, as before.

groups.title: expected.md is the source of the rubric lists
groups.why: The grader and the cases both need one definition of what a Must, Good, and Must not item is, and the [brief](source:s1) asked for one source of truth a human can edit.
groups.summary: parseExpectedMd in scripts/eval/case.ts reads the bullets under the three headings that eval/review-criteria.md defines, and listEvalCases hands them to the runner as a Rubric beside the case spec.
lookFor: A case folder with no expected.md gets three empty lists and runs on; an expected.md that lacks one of the three headings throws from loadEvalCase, which fails every eval run the way a broken case.json does.
Only lines that start with a dash and a space under a heading count. A bullet wrapped onto a second line keeps only its first line.

groups.title: One rubric grader call per case
groups.why: The grouping and prose graders produced open-ended findings that measured grader verbosity as much as review quality [session](source:s1).
groups.summary: runRubricGrader in scripts/eval/graders.ts sends the packet plus the numbered lists and the review's lookFor bullets, and parseRubricReply zips the model's positional yes or no arrays back onto the item text that run.ts passes in.
lookFor: The call is skipped when the rubric and the bullet list are both empty, so that case has no rubric.json and no must, good, mustNot, or bullets counts on its line.
A reply with the wrong entry count is a parse error: the grader retries once with the reason appended, and a second failure records rubric parse FAIL with empty output instead of failing the case.

The prompt caps work-tree reads at four files for the bullet checks. Search calls are not reads, so cigster-99 still made 6 to 8 tool calls per pass and 850k to 1.2M raw tokens, most of them cache reads of the 344 kB packet.
--rescore now runs the grader, so it needs MUSE_CODE_API_KEY unless --no-graders is also passed. skillSection and readNextSkillMd in scripts/eval/skill.ts had no caller left and are gone.

groups.title: Case line, deltas, totals, and report show the rubric counts
groups.why: Every consumer of CaseResult read grouping, prose, and claims, which no longer exist [session](source:s1).
groups.summary: CaseResult in scripts/eval/result.ts carries one rubric field, and formatCaseLine, formatBaselineDelta, formatRunTotals, and rubricHtml in report.ts all count it through rubricCounts.
lookFor: formatBaselineDelta prints must, good, mustNot, and bullets deltas only when both the current and the previous result have a rubric; a run against a baseline from before this change prints only the check deltas.

groups.title: Summary lints replace the prose grader
groups.why: The [brief](source:s1) asked for prose quality to become lints where it can.
groups.summary: proseLints in scripts/eval/checks.ts counts sentences and path-like tokens in the document summary and each group summary next to the existing dash and sentence-length lints.
lookFor: A path token is either a slash path or a word of two or more characters with a one-to-five letter extension, so foo.ts and a/b count and e.g does not; more than three in one summary lints. Sentences split on a period, question mark, or exclamation mark followed by a space, so e.g. x counts as two.
Lints stay advisory: in 133 saved reviews the two new lints fired 19 times.

groups.title: Every expected.md rewritten from its pull request
groups.why: None of the eleven files were written by a human, and the [brief](source:s1) asked for a rewrite by a trusted model with every Must claim verified at head.
groups.summary: Each expected.md follows the template in eval/review-criteria.md with Must, Good, Must not, and Notes written from the frozen sources, the diff, and the code at head, and its case.json loses claims and gains the pairs its Groups section implies.
lookFor: Three old claims were wrong or misleading and are now Must not items: flask's cookie fix is the hostname parse, not the localhost fallback; ruff's frozen issue file is an unrelated ruff PR about PrinterFlag; starship's config-schema.json entry is stale at head (definitions refs and a Vcs enum that does not match Vec<&str>).

Must items that packed two facts into one sentence flipped between grader passes (flask 0, 2, 0 of 3; cigster 5, 4, 3 of 5). The final items hold one fact each; a confirmation pass gave flask 3/3 and cigster 5/7 with the two judgment facts a clean no.
ruff-29024 size narrows to trivial or small and caddy, cobra, and comprehende-57 cap parts at 1. comprehende-59 gains sourceKinds pr and pr-comment, which fails a review that emits no pr source.

commits.subject: Eval: the grader accepts the main fact; shorter Must items
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
A Must item may carry more detail than the review. The grader answers
yes when the review gives the main fact and contradicts nothing. Long
compound items in cigster, caddy, and starship are split, with the
dropped detail moved to Good. Two together pairs and one apart pair
that most saved reviews failed on a judgment call are dropped.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Eval: rewrite every expected.md from the pull request
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
Each case now has Must, Good, and Must not lists that the grader reads
directly, written from the frozen sources, the diff, and the code at
head. case.json drops claims and gains together and apart pairs taken
from the Groups section.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Eval: one rubric grader per case, read from expected.md
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
The grouping and prose graders are gone. One read-only call gets the
review packet plus the Must, Good, and Must not lists from expected.md
and answers yes or no per item with a quote. It also marks each lookFor
bullet the review wrote as true or false at head. Deterministic checks
still decide pass or fail; summaries get sentence-count and path-list
lints. --rescore now regrades saved reviews.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
